compounds.//: Cleanup lives on each configuration, not here: VS Code ignores postDebugTask on a compound (the compound schema accepts only name, presentation, configurations, stopAll, preLaunchTask). stopAll is session-level and fires only on a *manual* stop.
compounds.name: Duct: App + API

compounds.//: The desktop stack with every agent turn, model call and tool call traced into Phoenix, and Phoenix's own MCP (.mcp.json → http://localhost:6006/mcp) up for an agent to query the traces. Phoenix is listed first so it is listening before the sidecar's first batch; the exporter would retry anyway, but the first turn's spans are the ones you launched this for. The API is the traced uvicorn variant so a browser tab against :8002 lands in the same trace store as the sidecar.
compounds.name: Duct: Desktop + API + Phoenix
configurations: Desktop: Duct Dev app (local env, traced)

compounds.//: Dev-variant bundle against a locally-run Railway-shaped API. Registered .app, so the sign-in deep link works.
compounds.name: Duct: Desktop + API

configurations.//: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is what turns agent tracing on (agents/core/telemetry.py::configure_tracing). Without it the Phoenix compound starts a trace UI that receives nothing.
configurations.name: Backend: FastAPI (uvicorn verbose)

configurations.//: Freezes the backend into backend/dist/duct-sidecar. Run this once, before the first desktop launch: a missing build ships a broken app. After that the desktop configurations refreeze it themselves when the backend has moved ahead (the npm pre* hooks), so this is for the first freeze and for forcing one. NOT plain `pyinstaller`: that deletes its output directory before rebuilding, which strips the binary and dylibs from under a sidecar the running app is executing. The script stages the freeze and swaps it in instead. Takes ~3 min.
configurations.name: Desktop: Build sidecar

configurations.//: Local-first desktop: the shell spawns the frozen sidecar on a loopback port and the web app repoints at it, so no uvicorn and no Railway. `dev:local` starts the Next dev server itself via beforeDevCommand. sidecar.rs falls back to backend/dist/duct-sidecar, so that freeze is what you get — `predev:local` refreezes it first when the backend is ahead, which costs ~3 min on the run after a backend change.
configurations.name: Desktop: Tauri dev (sidecar backend)

configurations.//: Builds the dev-variant bundle (own identifier + ai.getduct.desktop.dev scheme, so it coexists with TestFlight), waits for the Next dev server, then opens it against backend/.env.local. Unlike `tauri dev` this is a registered .app, so the sign-in deep link works. Rebuild is incremental (~15s); web changes still hot-reload. A backend change costs ~3 min more on the next run, because `prebuild:dev` refreezes the sidecar rather than bundling the old one. `open` hands the app to launchd, which does NOT inherit this shell's environment — hence `--env`, the only way the sidecar learns which env to embody. Keep that argument quoted: VS Code substitutes ${workspaceFolder} as literal text before the shell parses the line, so a workspace path containing a space otherwise splits into a bogus second file operand and a DUCT_ENV_FILE truncated at the space — which every Configs default then silently papers over. `--stderr` captures the app's log (including the sidecar's, relayed by sidecar.rs) where you can actually read it. NOTE: this session ends immediately, so Stop cannot close the app and no postDebugTask can be attached — quit it yourself, or run the 'Desktop: stop Duct Dev app' task. Force-quitting skips RunEvent::Exit and orphans its Python sidecar.
configurations.name: Desktop: Duct Dev app (local env)
configurations.command: npm run build:dev && until curl -sf http://localhost:3003 >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done && open --env "DUCT_ENV_FILE=${workspaceFolder}/backend/.env.local" --stderr /tmp/duct-desktop.log 'src-tauri/target/debug/bundle/macos/Duct Dev.app' && echo 'log: tail -f /tmp/duct-desktop.log'

configurations.//: The local-env launch above, with the sidecar exporting spans to Phoenix on :6006. A second `--env` is the only way in: launchd does not inherit this shell, and putting OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT in .env.local would turn tracing on for every desktop launch and log an export failure per batch whenever Phoenix is not running. `open --env` may be repeated (it rejects only single-letter names). Part of the 'Duct: Desktop + API + Phoenix' compound; on its own, start Phoenix first or the spans go nowhere.
configurations.name: Desktop: Duct Dev app (local env, traced)
configurations.command: npm run build:dev && until curl -sf http://localhost:3003 >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done && open --env "DUCT_ENV_FILE=${workspaceFolder}/backend/.env.local" --env "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:6006" --stderr /tmp/duct-desktop.log 'src-tauri/target/debug/bundle/macos/Duct Dev.app' && echo 'log: tail -f /tmp/duct-desktop.log · traces: http://localhost:6006'

configurations.//: Same bundle, same window (localhost:3003), but the sidecar embodies backend/.env.prod — so it reads and WRITES the production database. The frontend stays local on purpose: the deployed app.getduct.ai build registers the `ai.getduct.desktop` scheme, not this bundle's `.dev` one, so pointing the window at it would break the sign-in deep link. Use this to reproduce something that only happens on prod data; prefer the local env for everything else.
configurations.name: Desktop: Duct Dev app (prod env)
configurations.command: npm run build:dev && until curl -sf http://localhost:3003 >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done && open --env "DUCT_ENV_FILE=${workspaceFolder}/backend/.env.prod" --stderr /tmp/duct-desktop.log 'src-tauri/target/debug/bundle/macos/Duct Dev.app' && echo 'log: tail -f /tmp/duct-desktop.log'
